title: Longest Balanced Substring After One Swap
summary: Given a binary string, you can swap two characters at most once to form a balanced substring.
statement: Given a binary string, you can swap two characters at most once to form a balanced substring. Determine the longest balanced substring possible after the swap.
constraints: s is a nonempty binary string.
You may swap any two positions at most once, including positions outside the chosen substring.
Return the greatest substring length containing equal numbers of zeroes and ones after the swap.
hints: Encode one as +1 and zero as -1; balanced substrings have prefix difference zero.
One cross-boundary swap can repair a substring whose difference is ±2, provided the needed opposite bit exists outside it.
Store occurrence indices for each prefix value, using the earliest feasible boundary and a second boundary when the earliest consumes all available bits.
The three checked differences 0 and ±2 are exactly the changes achievable by at most one swap.
editorial: The three checked differences 0 and ±2 are exactly the changes achievable by at most one swap.

tests.explanation: Swap one endpoint one with an interior zero to obtain a balanced substring of length four.
The whole string is already balanced, so the answer is two.
